subject: general
question: The seeds of which plant of the Fabaceae family are used as a spice, flavouring agent and food supplement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Trigonella foenum graecum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Trigonella foenum graecum**, commonly known as fenugreek, belongs to the Fabaceae family and is extensively used in cooking as a spice and flavoring agent.
 
• Fenugreek seeds are rich in nutrients such as protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals like iron and magnesium, making them valuable as a food supplement.
 
• It is widely used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including improving digestion, reducing inflammation, and managing blood sugar levels.
 
• Fenugreek seeds have a distinct aroma and are used in various cuisines worldwide, particularly in Indian, Middle Eastern, and Mediterranean dishes.
 
• The plant is also known for its agricultural importance as it helps improve soil fertility by fixing nitrogen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dolichos oleifera lablab:**

 
 
• Commonly known as hyacinth bean, it is a climbing plant used as a vegetable and fodder crop.
 
• It is not typically used as a spice or flavoring agent but is consumed in its immature pod form as a vegetable in certain cuisines.
 
 
 
• **Cajanus cajan:**
 
 
• Also known as pigeon pea, it is a legume widely cultivated for its edible seeds.
 
• Pigeon peas are a staple in many tropical and subtropical regions, often used in soups, stews, and curries.
 
• Unlike fenugreek, it is not used as a spice or flavoring agent.
 
 
 
• **Arachis hypogea:**
 
 
• Commonly known as the peanut or groundnut, it is a legume grown for its edible seeds.
 
• Peanuts are used to produce oil, butter, and flour and are consumed as snacks or in various culinary preparations.
 
• They are not used as a spice but are valued for their high protein and fat content.
